q: 1. The cement becomes useless if it absorbed moisture more than
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration begins prematurely inside the bag, forming lumps and losing its binding strength, making it unfit for use.

q: 2. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Lime stone (calcareous material) supplies the required lime (CaO) content, which forms the major ingredient of cement, hence it is the commonly used raw material.

q: 3. The bulk density of aggregates is generally expressed as
explain: As per IS 2386, bulk density of aggregate is determined using a measuring cylinder of known litre capacity, so it is conventionally reported in kg per litre.

q: 4. To obtain cement dry powder, lime stones and shales or their slurry, is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix is burnt at 1400°C–1500°C, the clinkering temperature, at which the raw materials fuse to form cement clinker.

q: 5. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted are
explain: Rounded/spherical aggregates pack together most efficiently for a given size, leaving the least void space compared to irregular, angular or flaky shapes.

q: 6. How much cement contained in one bag
explain: A standard bag of cement weighs 50 kg, which corresponds to a weight (force) of about 500 N (50 × 9.81 ≈ 490.5 N ≈ 500 N).

q: 7. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of coarser particles relative to fines reduces the paste's ability to lubricate the mix, making the concrete harsh and difficult to work.

q: 8. The maximum quantity of ingredients present in cement production is
explain: Lime (CaO) forms the largest proportion (about 60-65%) of the chemical composition of cement, hence it is present in maximum quantity.

q: 9. Ferro-concrete is another name given to (Ferror = iron)
explain: Ferro-concrete literally means iron-concrete, referring to concrete reinforced with steel (iron) bars, i.e., reinforced cement concrete.

q: 10. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is
explain: Iron oxide is present in the smallest percentage (about 3-4%) among the major ingredients (lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide) of cement.

q: 11. Reinforced cement concrete is equally strong in taking
explain: By combining concrete (strong in compression) with steel reinforcement (strong in tension) and proper detailing for shear, RCC is designed to resist tensile, compressive, and shear stresses effectively.

q: 12. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Magnesium oxide is a minor constituent and is present in the least percentage (about 1-3%) among all chemical ingredients of cement; its excess makes cement unsound.

q: 13. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use, is called
explain: Prestressed concrete has internal compressive stresses artificially induced (via tensioned tendons) before loading, so that tensile stresses from service loads are offset.

q: 14. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: The typical proportion of ingredients in cement is Lime 63%, Silica 22%, Alumina 6%, and Iron oxide 3%.

q: 15. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking refers to the increase in volume of a given mass of sand due to the film of water surrounding each particle pushing them apart, i.e., swelling of sand when wetted with moisture up to a certain limit.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: lime in excess, causes the cement to expand and disintegrate
silica in excess, causes the cement to set slowly
alumina in excess, reduces the strength of the cement
magnesium oxide in excess, remains in free state and makes the cement unsound
explain: All the listed effects of excess lime, silica, alumina, and magnesium oxide are correct statements regarding their influence on cement properties.

q: 17. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Limestone (calcareous material, source of lime/CaO) is the principal raw material used along with clay in cement manufacture.

q: 18. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
explain: Excess alkalis in cement react with atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, forming soluble salts that migrate to the surface, causing efflorescence (white deposits).

q: 19. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: OPC clinker is produced by burning a mixture of calcareous material (limestone) and argillaceous material (clay) in a kiln, then grinding with gypsum.

q: 20. In making precast structural units for partition and wall lining purposes, the concrete should be
explain: Light-weight concrete is preferred for precast partition and lining units because it reduces dead load while still providing adequate strength and insulation.

q: 21. The characteristic, which makes the concrete a versatile and widely used material of modern construction, is the possibility of
options: controlling the properties of concrete by using appropriate ingredients
molding the concrete in any desired shape
complete mechanization of concrete preparation and its placing process
explain: Concrete's versatility comes from a combination of factors: controllable properties through mix design, moldability into any shape, and full mechanization of production and placement, all of which together make it widely used.

q: 22. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following :
options: gypsum in cement decreases the setting time
the first compound of cement which reacts with water, is C2S
bulking of sand is less when its particles are fine
explain: All three statements are actually incorrect: gypsum increases (not decreases) setting time, C3A (not C2S) reacts first with water, and bulking of sand is more (not less) when particles are fine. Hence 'all of the above' is the correct choice for incorrect statements.

q: 23. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture of silicious, argillaceous (clayey), and calcareous (limestone) materials together.

q: 24. The mixture of different ingredients of cement, is burnt at
explain: The raw mixture of cement ingredients is burnt at approximately 1400°C, the clinkering temperature, to form cement clinker.

q: 25. Le chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures expansion of a cement paste specimen to check for soundness, i.e., freedom from excessive free lime or magnesia that could cause unsoundness.

q: 26. The cement whose strength is little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement develops strength slowly at early stages due to lower C3S and C3A content, but eventually catches up with the strength of ordinary cement after about three months.

q: 27. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard test performed exclusively on fresh concrete to assess its workability.

q: 28. Volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: For a 1:2:4 mix (7 parts total, with dry volume factor ~1.54-1.55), the coarse aggregate proportion (4/7) of the total dry volume works out to approximately 84m3 for 100m3 of finished concrete.

q: 29. Particles of 0.002 mm size are that of
explain: By particle-size classification, particles finer than about 0.002 mm fall in the clay size range, distinct from silt, sand and gravel.

q: 30. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at a temperature between
explain: In the kiln, the raw mixture of calcareous (limestone) and argillaceous (clay) materials is burnt at very high temperatures of about 1500°C to 1600°C to form clinker.

q: 31. For quality control of portland cement, the test essentially done is
explain: Quality control of Portland cement requires testing setting time, soundness, tensile/compressive strength, and consistency, hence all of these are essential.

q: 32. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with clinker specifically to control/retard the otherwise flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 33. The chemical ingredient of cement which provides quick setting property to the cement is
explain: Alumina in cement lowers the clinkering temperature and imparts quick setting properties, though excess alumina can weaken the cement.

q: 34. Sieve analysis of portland cement is performed on IS sieve No.
explain: Fineness of Portland cement is tested by sieving on IS Sieve No. 9 (90 micron sieve) as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 35. The mixture of different ingredients of cement is burnt at
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at about 1400-1500°C to form clinker, and the closest listed value is 1400°C.

q: 36. The gypsum is added to the cement for
options: providing high strength to the cement
controlling the initial setting time of cement
lowering the initial setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard/control the initial setting time of cement, preventing flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 37. During manufacturing process of portland cement, gypsum or plaster of paris is added
options: to increase the strength of cement
to modify the colour of cement
to adjust the setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added to cement clinker to control/retard the fast setting action of tricalcium aluminate (C3A), thereby adjusting the setting time of cement.

q: 38. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during first three months but attains afterwards the same strength is known as
explain: Rapid hardening cement is formulated to gain high early strength; per this question's textbook description its early-age strength profile before catching up is attributed to rapid hardening portland cement.

q: 39. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, caused the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement makes the cement set slowly, as it increases the proportion of dicalcium silicate which hydrates and hardens slowly.

q: 40. The percentage of gypsum added to the clinker during manufacturing process is
explain: Gypsum is typically added in the range of 0.35% to 5.0% by weight of clinker to regulate the setting time of cement.

q: 41. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to is
explain: Portland pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate/chloride attack from sea water due to reduced permeability and lower free lime, making it preferable for marine structures.

q: 42. Lime when added in excess quantity
options: caused the cement to expand and disintegrate
lowers the clinkering temperature of cement
explain: Excess free lime in cement remains uncombined, and upon hydration it expands, causing the cement to become unsound and disintegrate.

q: 43. The initial and final setting time for OPC are approximately related as
explain: As per empirical relations used in the textbook, the final setting time (T) of OPC is approximately related to initial setting time (t) as T = 530 + t.

q: 44. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved thought IS sieve number
explain: IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) is used to check the fineness of finely ground cement after the grinding process is complete.

q: 45. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and thereby decreasing the setting time of cement.

q: 46. The diameter of needle in vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: For the initial setting time test, the Vicat needle used has a cross-sectional diameter of 1 mm as per IS specifications.

q: 47. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to the excess of
explain: Excess alkalies in cement react with moisture and carbon dioxide, migrating to the surface and crystallizing as a white efflorescence deposit.

q: 48. The minimum initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS code, the minimum initial setting time specified for ordinary Portland cement is 30 minutes.

q: 49. If the angularity number of aggregate is increased, then the workability of concrete using this aggregate will
explain: A higher angularity number indicates more angular (less rounded) aggregate with greater interlocking and friction, which reduces the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 50. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary portland cement, causes
options: reduction in chemical action with sulphates
explain: Addition of pozzolana affects cement in all these ways: it lowers early strength, reduces sulphate attack, increases shrinkage slightly, and reduces bleeding, hence all statements are correct.
